evidence.claim: Defines finite material/property vocabulary and mutable global feature list; clear discards current parsed features.
Reads physical word neighbors through MF_code, follows two directions or a supplied direction, collects multiword feature candidates; host enumeration/call schedule outside Lua.
Uses first three words to match property/verb phrase and returns matching subjects; this is not retail full NOT/AND/conditional grammar.
Queries controlled subjects and applies movement to actual host-returned actor IDs; slipping checks can alter command response.
Recursively pushes obstacles/text and calls MF_update only on unobstructed branch; no item/currency/stamina debit in this visible Lua path.
Stops or pushes according to current parsed subject properties; text defaults to push through nonnil branch; boundaries from host obstacle query.
Autonomous move/slip, push and sink consumers; sink removes both object and contacting sink through host callbacks.
Control/win/kill and hot/melt contact paths call actual host win/remove functions; exact engine scheduling/transaction semantics not present.
Three-word noun identity rule validates material names then calls MF_convert; persistent mutation/rollback/equipment behavior outside visible Lua.
Direction rotation, tile vocabulary and identity matching helpers; includes a NOT tile but not a demonstrated retail negation parser.

traces.prerequisite: Physical word positions produce a parsed feature list through opaque host word/position callbacks.
traces.decision: Manipulate word objects or move a controlled actor; configuration can make an object blocking/pushable, lethal/melting or a goal. The local rule-rebuild call schedule is not in Lua.
traces.cost: Input moves/opportunity and board constraints; no currency/material/stamina cost or native paid duration in selected Lua. Do not infer whole-game zero cost or undo semantics.
traces.mutation: MF_update positional movement; MF_remove and MF_win requested at contacts after selected property tests.
traces.consumer: Parsed rule lookup feeds movement obstruction, control and contact effect functions.
traces.failureAfternath: Blocking prevents movement; sink requests removal of both contacts, hot/melt removal of affected object, kill removes player, goal callback. Actual host callback lifecycle/save/undo/order unknown.

adaptation.name: One local formation with physical clauses
adaptation.flow: Acquire owned reusable plates/site permission -> pay setup/effort -> select one bounded supported arrangement -> derived local environment/access function -> actual useful paid action -> break/rearrange/expiry with retained material and consequence.
adaptation.cost: Author finite real means; no general free semantic effect strings.
constraints: No changing custody/ownership or redefining victory
Reserved setup cannot change during dependent accepted work
Versioned arrangement and current definition identity
observableGate: Two configurations alter a supported useful action/risk using same conserved plates
Removing one physical clause removes future support without undoing completed output
Observer sees learned clause and reported effect, not hidden world truth
Later authorised generated-fixture save/failure gate preserves exact setup and paid costs

largerImplications: Discovery of permitted interactions can change the rules available to the same character, rather than only numerical stats.
Spatial word placement is functional in Baba; a native command/table can demonstrate YAIRPG clause choices before a renderer.
World-scoped authoring can permit local laws/formation exceptions while keeping identity, knowledge and custody global owners.
Property configuration and identity transformation need different conservation/removal policies.
Local reversible experimentation is not general historical rewind or save rollback.
effort: medium-to-high new arrangement/consumer/validation/observer binding; bounded typed mappings easier than importing grammar/host engine
